# host-baselines.tsv — the per-host reference artifacts gate-p5 judges against.
# Tab-separated, tracked, human-diffable, and keyed on THE EXACT CPU-MODEL STRING
# gate-p5's README criterion greps (`remote_probe | cut -d'|' -f1`). One key shared
# with the criterion that consumes it, so the registry can never disagree with the
# check about who a host is.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A criterion whose reference artifact predates the host's
# admission cannot judge that host: the bar-derivation set, the README row and the
# archived baseline are all artifacts of runs a newly admitted host was not in, and
# convicting it for its absence from them measures its admission date rather than
# its code. That is the BASELINE-REGISTERED class (ruled 2026-08-21, #6), and this
# file is what a host graduates INTO.
# THE GATE PROPOSES ROWS AND NEVER WRITES THIS FILE. An instrument minting the
# reference it will judge against is self-certification, so gate-p5 emits a fully
# formed candidate row to build/baseline-candidates-<rev>.tsv and stops there;
# landing it is a reviewed commit act, exactly like every reference artifact before
# it. The three states it decides between come from the archive, not from a flag:
#   registered   — a row here → judged at (baseline - BASELINE_MARGIN), derivation printed
#   new          — no row, and no archived judged log for this host predating the run
#                  → BASELINE: verdict green-compatible, candidate emitted
#   owing        — no row, but a prior archived judged log exists → FAIL, naming the
#                  unmet registration
# BASELINE IS SINGLE-SHOT PER HOST BY CONSTRUCTION: the run that renders it creates
# the prior log that forbids it next time, so no host can ride the exemption. The
# scope of that guarantee is stated where it is weaker than it sounds — see
# `baseline_prior` in scripts/gate-lib.sh.
# BASELINES ARE IMMUTABLE except by the two doors that already exist in law:
# supersession by a tighter re-measure, or dated re-registration citing a named code
# change. Either way the row's estimator, source and grounds move with the value;
# provenance is the row, not a footnote.
# NOT IN HERE, on purpose: the three CPU models that DERIVED CEIL_FRACTION
# (gate-p5.sh's CEIL_DERIVED_FROM). Their reference artifact does not predate their
# admission — they are the artifact — so they stay on the fleet bar. Per-host
# convergence for them is a post-tag option, not something smuggled in with this
# mechanism.
# THERE ARE NO DATA ROWS YET, and that is a measurement state rather than an
# oversight. keel-skx is the one host owing registration, and its share baseline
# cannot be imported from the free-instrument runs that measured it (5ec5fea,
# 33de3b2): a published reference is an estimator, never a draw (§5 rule 16), and
# both of those are single draws under the instrument the pinning transition
# replaces. Its rows are born from the pinned arm of that campaign (#6).
# columns, tab-separated:
#   1 cpu_model  the exact string the host reports, as gate-p5 greps it
#   2 criterion  what the baseline is a baseline FOR (e.g. share/Sgemm, scale/Strsm)
#   3 baseline   the reference value; the bar is this less BASELINE_MARGIN
#   4 estimator  how it was reduced from samples, with N and the runs named
#   5 source     the archived log the value is recomputable from
#   6 as_of      the date the row was landed
#   7 grounds    why this host has its own baseline rather than the fleet's
